landing_text:
The Critters are a peace-loving, yet unknown colony living in the forest. Lately, a disease has caused some of them to turn into mutants disturbing the peace. Mutated Critters go on a rampage and stop obliging the colony's rules. Since the Critters are unable to distinguish mutants from healthy Critters, they need your help! On the way to a save tower, they behave according to certain rules the mutants ignore. They have developed a device that, when operated correctly, relocates the mutants to a save place until a cure has been found.

Help to save the peace by creating portals that test the Critter‘s properties. If a Critter passes the test, it will proceed to the tower. Increase your score by letting healthy Critters reach home and relocating mutated ones. Decrease your score by letting mutants reach the tower. To help you know the correct behaviour, you are given the rules according to which the Critters behave. Start with the first level or select another level.
landing_text_new:
The Critters are a peace-loving, yet unknown colony living in the forest. Lately, a disease has caused some of them to turn into mutants disturbing the peace. Mutated Critters go on a rampage and stop obliging the colony's rules. The healthy Critters want to flee to a safe tower to avoid being infected. But they need your help! They have developed a device that, when operated correctly, relocates the mutants to a save place.

Help to save the peace by creating portals that test the Critters' properties and only allow healthy Critters to continue on the path. Start with the first level or select another level.

Once the Critters have made it to the tower, they seek advice from a wise wizard to heal their sick friends. He decides to help them and brew them a healing potion. In order to do so, he needs the Critters to bring him magic berries, which only grow in long neglected regions. He provides the Critters with instructions and a collection basked and sends them on their journey. It is not easy to keep the wizard's notes intact on the arduous paths, which is why some Critters have smudged, incorrect instructions.

This is where they need your help! Send the critters with the wrong instructions back to the wizard. To do this, use the signposts along the path and test for the Critters' berries.

privacy_text: Code Critters collects only an email address and no other personal information through the user registration page. The email address, together with username and password can be viewed on this profile page. The score data for the individual levels is also stored. Code Critters will not share private information with other companies. Anonymised game data may be used for scientific analysis. Code Critters uses the email address only for authentication, and to allow users to reset their passwords. Code Critters does not actively send any information to your email address. Code Critters uses cookies for logins. The login cookie is deleted when the browser session is closed. This privacy notice was last updated on October 15, 2020. If you have any questions about Code Critters' privacy policy, the data we hold on you, or you would like to exercise one of your data protection rights, please do not hesitate to contact us via email: gordon.fraser@uni-passau.de or via our postal address: Chair of Software Engineering II, University of Passau, Innstrasse 33, D-94032 Passau, Germany.
project_text: The Code Critters project aims at teaching children about mutation testing using a gamification approach. The web application was developed at the University of Passau within the scope of a bachelor's thesis at the chair of Software Engineering II.

hint_level_1_intro_0: Alright. Let's start with a little introduction.
hint_level_1_intro_1: On the right you see the code that needs to be tested. It describes the usual behavior of a critter, if not infected.
hint_level_1_intro_2: Here on the left is the critters' village affected by the disease outbreak where the critters flee from.
hint_level_1_intro_3: And they want to make it to the safe tower. But only the healthy ones should arrive at the tower.
hint_level_1_intro_4: You can help the critters by building portals that collect all the infected critters along the way. Let's start by building such a portal. Click on any field along the critters' path.
hint_level_1_intro_5: Super! You can use the blocks on the left and connect them to check the critters' behavior. Let's start with your first test! Use the 'only critters with ... equals ... can pass' block and drag it into the portal.
hint_level_1_intro_6: Great! With the help of portals it is now on you to decide which critters should be collected, and which are still healthy. In the beginning a healthy critter behaves as described in the Initialization part...
hint_level_1_intro_7: And on each tile of the gameboard along his way he executes the exact behavior that is described in the Executed code on each tile part.
hint_level_1_intro_8: To ensure that you collect all the infected critters, you have to check the entire behavior. Try to create your first portal!
hint_level_1_first_0: The code describes the critter's behavior if he is not infected. It contains two parts that need to be tested.
hint_level_1_first_1: Let's take a closer look at the Initialization part. It holds the initial behavior of a critter when he leaves the village.
hint_level_1_first_2: A good place for the first testing portal would be on some field right after the village, for example here. Click on the field to open the toolbox.
hint_level_1_first_3: Can you fill the portal? Or do you need a little help to start? Continue to see the start of a test.
hint_level_1_first_4: Now you can try to finish the portal and make sure to let only the healthy critters pass. You can save it there when you are done.
hint_level_2_first_0: Your task is to thoroughly test the behavior of the critter (code on the right).
hint_level_2_first_1: To test the complete behavior, you need to understand both code parts. The initial behavior of the critters is described in the Initialization part.
hint_level_2_first_2: And in the Executed code on each tile part describes their behavior along the way. Have a closer look at it!
hint_level_2_first_3: On which fields should the critters still look like described in the Initialization part? Click on the appropriate field to build a test portal for the initial behavior!
hint_level_2_first_4: Great! Do you know how to fill the portal? Continue if you would like me to help you with a good start.
hint_level_2_first_5: Now you can try to finish the portal and make sure to let only the healthy critters pass.
hint_level_3_first_0: In this level, there is only the Executed code on each tile code. However, it clearly states how the critters behave along the path.
hint_level_3_first_1: Depending on the terrain the critter is on, he wears a specific shirt color.
hint_level_3_first_2: Can you find out which shirt color a critter should have at the beginning on this field? Click on it and give it a try!
hint_level_3_first_3: Now you can try to build a test portal using the 'only critters with ... equals ... can pass'. If you need some help to get started, click further...
hint_level_3_first_4: Complete the portal and let only the critters with the correct shirt color through!
hint_level_4_first_0: In this level there are two paths. But the Executed code on each tile code clearly describes how the critters should behave along the path.
hint_level_4_first_1: The critters shirt color depends on the terrain and the x-coordinates of the field on which the critter walks.
hint_level_4_first_2: Do you know which shirt color the critters should wear on this field? Click on it!
hint_level_4_first_3: Take a look at the code again! What shirtcolor is correct on a dirt field? Fill the portal with the right color!
hint_level_4_first_4: Great! And don't forget to save the portal here!
hint_level_4_first_5: Done! Now we should make sure that only as soon as the critters walk on the dirt, do they change into a red shirt...
hint_level_4_first_6: Let's use this field! Click on it to build a portal!
hint_level_4_first_7: Which shirt color is the right one here? Fill the portal and the upper path is secured! I'm sure you can build the remaining portals to secure the lower path too!
hint_level_5_first_0: Let's take a closer look at the code of a healthy Critter. Their shirt color along the way depends on two things...
hint_level_5_first_1: Firstly, it matters on which terrain the Critter walks...
hint_level_5_first_2: And secondly, it matters on which Y-coordinate of the game field he walks.
hint_level_5_first_3: That means, on fields with y-coordinate equal to 13, the Critters should change their shirt color. Let's take care of that right away! Click on a field with y-coordinate equal to 13, for example there.
hint_level_5_first_4: Fill the test portal with the correct shirt color for this field!
hint_level_5_first_5: Great! You can save it like this!
hint_level_5_first_6: Done! Now you need similar test portals for the rest of the code. On which fields along the way should they wear a red shirt, and where a green one?
hint_level_6_first_0: Let's take a look at the code of a healthy critter. The special feature in this level is the new block 'variable count'.
hint_level_6_first_1: Similar to the previous shirt and hair colors, you can understand this 'variable count' block as a property of the critters.
hint_level_6_first_2: The difference is, this block doesn't represent a color, but a number. You can see this in the Initialization: count is equal to 0 at the beginning.
hint_level_6_first_3: And in the Executed code on each tile part, you can see that the 'variable count' changes along the way. On dirty ground, the count is always increased by 1.
hint_level_6_first_4: If you read the code carefully, you can figure out the value of 'variable count' for each field.
hint_level_6_first_5: Let's look at this first dirt field. Click on it to build a test portal.
hint_level_6_first_6: Do you already know what number the 'variable count' must have here? Fill the correct number in the gap!
hint_level_6_first_7: Great! You can save it like this!
hint_level_6_first_8: Now you can think about what number the 'variable count' has on other fields, and build more portals there. For example, what does it look like on the last dirt field?
hint_level_7_first_0: In this level, the critters start off from their village on the right...
hint_level_7_first_1: ... and with a specific hair color! This is specified in the Initialization part.
hint_level_7_first_2: The hair color of the critters changes depending on which field they are on. You can find this in the Executed code on each tile part.
hint_level_7_first_3: When which hair color should be used depends on two things: the terrain and the x-coordinate of the field.
hint_level_7_first_4: Let's look at this field. Since it has dirt as terrain, the red highlighted code applies here. Click on the field to build a test portal!
hint_level_7_first_5: Look at the code again and insert the correct hair color!
hint_level_7_first_6: Great! Now save the test portal!
hint_level_7_first_7: Next, you can think about where the critters will change to a different hair color. For example, what is it here?
hint_level_8_first_0: Let's take a look at the code of the healthy critters. Here in the Initialization part, it describes with which properties the critters start from the village.
hint_level_8_first_1: In this level, there are two properties: the 'variable count' and the shirt color.
hint_level_8_first_2: Have you already played Level 6? The 'variable count' appears there too. If not, it's best to play it first. Otherwise, let's go through this code here together...
hint_level_8_first_3: In the Executed code on each tile part, the 'variable count' is always increased by 1. But only starting from a certain x-coordinate!
hint_level_8_first_4: And on which field is the 'variable count' then equal to 5? This is how you can find out on which field the shirt color of the critters must change to light blue!
hint_level_8_first_5: Should we start building a test for the starting properties of the critters together? Then click to continue...
hint_level_8_first_6: Click on this field to build a first test portal!
hint_level_8_first_7: You can directly test both properties in one portal! Now you can think about how to complete the test. I'm sure you know it!
hint_level_9_first_0: Let's look at the code of the healthy critters together. If you've already done Level 6 and Level 8, you're already familiar with the 'variable count' by now.
hint_level_9_first_1: As in the other levels, the 'variable count' is initially equal to 0...
hint_level_9_first_2: And in the Executed code on each tile part, it states that the 'variable count' is either increased by 2 or by 1...
hint_level_9_first_4: You now need to figure out and test what value the 'variable count' has on which field. Look closely at what the x-coordinate and y-coordinate of a field are! Do you need some more help? Then click to continue.
hint_level_9_first_5: As you can see in the code, on every field with an x-coordinate greater than or equal to 4, either 2 or 1 is added to the 'variable count'. Let's build a portal on this field, click on it!
hint_level_9_first_6: Insert the correct number for 'variable count' at this spot. Look closely at the x- and y-coordinates of the field.
hint_level_9_first_7: Great, you can save the test portal like this.
hint_level_9_first_8: To catch all mutants, you can now think about what number the 'variable count' must have on a later field. What is it here, for example? You can surely figure this out!
hint_level_10_first_0: Let's take a look at the code together. In the Initialization, it says that the critters should wear an orange shirt at the beginning.
hint_level_10_first_1: And along their way, the critters change their shirt color several times. To find out which shirt color they should wear on which fields, you need to examine the code closely.
hint_level_10_first_2: For the red shirt color, the X-coordinate OR the terrain of a field is important.
hint_level_10_first_3: And if the shirt on the respective field is not supposed to be red, then the next step is to check the code for the blue shirt. Do you know what to do? Or should we build a portal together? Then click next.
hint_level_10_first_4: Let's take this field. Click on it and build a portal!
hint_level_10_first_5: Check out the code and set the correct shirt color for this field!
hint_level_10_first_6: Great! Now just save it.
hint_level_10_first_7: Now there are still portals missing to secure the rest of the path. Do the critters start with the correct orange shirt color? And on which part of the path do they wear the blue shirt? You will surely find out!
